title: Framing the problem: prediction, decision, and the cost of each kind of error

videos.script: A subscription company asks for a churn model. {{request}} It sounds like a specification. It is not one yet. A model produces a number. The business has to do something with it. {{number}} Here, the something is a credit of forty reais, sent at the start of the month. {{credit}} Send it to someone about to leave, and some of them stay. Send it to someone who was staying anyway, and the money is gone. {{two-errors}} Those are two different mistakes. They cost different amounts. And no metric in any library knows what they cost. {{costs}} So this lesson fits no model at all. It builds the lab you will use for the whole course, on your own computer. {{lab}} It makes the data, from one program you can read. And it asks four questions before anything is trained. What is one row. When is the prediction made. What exactly is predicted. And what will be done with the answer. {{questions}} Get those wrong, and the best model in the world answers the wrong question. {{end}}
